I quit about 7 years ago. These are the things that worked for me..

1) I didn't tell anyone, I didn't make a big announcement. I just did it quietly by myself. If I failed no one would no, so I didn't have any external pressure on me. iINo one asking me how it's going all the time. If I was asked why I wasn't going for a smoke, I just said I don't want to right now.

2) I set basic rules for myself. No smoking in the car. No smoking in the house. Not only did it make my house and car smell better, it made each ciggarette a concious act, I had to get up and go have a cigarette, thirty made me more concious of my smoking, which had just become an automatic habit.

3) I looked at my smoking routine. When did I smoke? What made pull out a cigarette? I was smoking about a pack a day. I had a coffee and cigarette when I woke up, another coffee and cigarette before work, another at morning break, 2 at lunch, afternoon break, another after work. Then again when I got home. 1 before dinner, 1 after dinner. I smoked the most after dinner, when I was bored watching TV or gaming etc. Then a final cigarette before bed. It was a pretty regular routine.

4) Patches and Lozenges. I started with the 21mg patch, which I think is the highest, and 2mg Lozenges. The back of the shoulder blade or on my waist on the side under my belt worked for me (I sweat at work and my belt helped keep the patch on). I didn't just stop smoking immediately. I used the patched then one by one I replaced my cigarettes with lozenges. The first few weeks I was still smoking like 10 cigarettes a day. but as the days went by I slowly replaced cigarettes with lozenges. I'd put off a scheduled cigarette and have a lozenge and just hold out for the next scheduled cigarette.

I also realised I was smoking more when I was bored, so I found things to keep busy at those times.

Eventually I got to the point that I will was only smoking about 3 cigarettes a day Then one day I just didn't want to anymore.

It took about 3 months from start to finish. I kept going with the lozenges for another couple of months, but dropped the patches a few weeks after my last cigarette.

Then over a month or so I started one by one replacing the (mint) nicotine lozenges with peppermints.

Best of luck friend. I hope I've helped.
